label: copy-phase input c (orig pos ~2) when next output is c or 2, mid-length long sequences
explanation: Very sparse feature that fires only in the copy phase, and only when the fed-back input is the letter c (100% of activations; in_first=0, so this c is being re-read from the original). Most of the mass comes from c sitting at original position ~2 (recall_idx 3 holds 76% of mass, 2-4 holds 98%), with the output at that step being c (a repeated cc) or 2 (63% and 26% of mass). It favours long sequences (L=9 holds 53% of mass, almost none for L<=5) with 3-5 outputs still to go. The strongest examples are cc / c2 bigrams at positions 2-3 of 7-9 token sequences. Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, or on any input token other than c. The predicate captures about 82% of the mass on dev, but precision is low (~12%): most c-input copy steps matching these conditions stay silent, and no simple variable I tested (later-token context such as h, next_out) separates them cleanly.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=c (+2.83), recall_idx=3 & in_tok=c (+2.42), in_tok=c (+2.31), phase=2 & out_tok=c (+2.13), out_tok=c (+2.07), phase=2 & out_tok=2 (+1.83). Lower it: orig5=- (-1.93), prev_tok=3 (-1.77), orig8=- (-1.30), orig6=c (-1.30).
